text: Onions and garlic serve as fundamental flavor and aroma agents during food preparation. Chefs frequently sauté or fry these aromatics to provide a savory profile for items like stir-fries, omelets, and casseroles. Overuse should be avoided because excessive quantities can dominate other tastes. Preparation begins by washing the produce and removing all tough exterior layers. Next, cut the ingredients into small pieces and cook them in oil within a pan until they become translucent. The required duration ranges from several minutes to sixty minutes, contingent upon onion thickness and desired doneness. Once cooked, incorporate the mixture into recipes or use it for specific preparations such as Greek salad or roasted garlic potatoes. Mastery comes with practice, allowing cooks to prepare numerous meals featuring these staples.
